candidate_relations.reason: The clinical course — rapid necrotic expansion despite appropriate antibiotics, negative blood cultures, and a swab growing S. epidermidis (likely contaminant/colonizer) — points away from a true pacemaker pocket infection toward pyoderma gangrenosum, a non-infectious neutrophilic dermatosis triggered by pathergy at the surgical site. The candidate asserts an infectious diagnosis incompatible with the reference diagnosis of pyoderma gangrenosum.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Infectious etiology vs. neutrophilic dermatosis (pyoderma gangrenosum)

case_quality_flags: Classic pathergy-triggered pyoderma gangrenosum post-pacemaker implantation; antibiotic failure and progressive necrosis despite treatment are key discriminating features against infectious pocket infection.
